ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To discuss or deliberate is to work something over in speech or thought, alone or with another person.
EvidenceBody: Nanquan says that he and Guizong have discussed phrases together and invites a capable participant to come out and discuss; Fengxue asks whether discussion belongs in the quarters or tea hall. Other speakers turn the same act into a warning. Dahui forbids reckless deliberation after the Second Patriarch’s bow and catalogues “needle-and-thread” discussions of an old case; Sanyi Mingyu rejects making Buddhist analysis of a rain display. Baoen Yuan says even “nothing-to-do discussion” is grit in the eye, while a verse speaks of ages spent deliberating. Zen does not give the word one stance: public consultation and the criticized working-over of cases are attested uses of the same act.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The records make deliberation itself a public topic: invited as encounter, located institutionally, catalogued as case interpretation, and rejected when it substitutes analysis for the event.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The word does not inherently mean mistaken conceptualization; several witnesses use it neutrally for discussion between participants.
